issues.title: feat(ui): the month review as a clipboard -- 3x the area, typeset, no longer covering the feed
issues.body:
## What Pip asked for

> "Month review -- can take up a lot more of the screen space, like, double or triple the area so we have something to work with. In fact, why don't we take this from green to having its own little UI elements - we're starting to promote some of them."

and then, mid-design:

> "the month review screen could come in, like, clipboard form or some other diegetic form"

## What it is now

**An object, not an overlay.** A hardboard clipboard with a metal clip holding a sheet of aged graph paper, and the month typed onto the sheet as a form.

The reasoning, so it can be argued with: the thesis of this game is that the bureaucracy **is** the game. A HUD panel says "here is your data". A sheet somebody clipped to a board and left on your desk says "here is what your month amounted to, and a person typed it up". The second one is the game's own argument. It is the same instinct as the 2026-08-12 calendar ruling ("semi-diegetic ... shrink or grow rather than disappear and reappear entirely"), so this is treated as a house register rather than a one-off -- see the new section in `godot/UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md`.

It also earns the modal. An object with physical presence has an obvious reason to sit on top of the feed, which is the cheapest honest fix for the occlusion complaint.

**Diegetic does not mean photorealistic here.** Every word on the sheet is set in `TerminalTheme.mono_font()` -- the same family as the WATCH feed and the plan screen. The paper is tinted down to office-light manila, not scanned-document white. It belongs to the dark office the isometric floor view implies.

### Layout

```
   +==============================================================================+
   |                            [====== clip ======]                              |
   | +--------------------------------------------------------------------------+ |
   | | Month Review                                              October 2017   | |   masthead, then a 2px rule
   | | ======================================================================== | |
   | | October 2017 begins.                                                     | |
   | |                                                                          | |
   | | | [!]  Attention: 20 fresh decisions this month (last month's unspent    | |   stamped left rule,
   | | |      reserve evaporated -- no banking).                                | |   translucent wash
   | |                                                                          | |
   | | Last month's movement           |  Rivals this month                     | |
   | | -------------------------       |  ------------------------------       | |
   | | Funds $1,119,896 -> $1,083,712  |  | DeepSafety            safety       | |
   | |                      [-$36,185] |  |   capabilities flat                | |
   | | Staff  3 -> 2              [-1] |  | CapabiliCorp    capabilities       | |
   | |                                 |  |   capabilities climbing fast       | |
   | |                                 |  | StealthAI (rumored)   balanced     | |
   | |                                 |  |   capabilities climbing fast       | |
   | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | |
   | | >>  Queue this month's actions, then press COMMIT THE MONTH to play the  | |
   | |     month out.                                                           | |
   | +--------------------------------------------------------------------------+ |
   |                                                                              |
   |                 [   Begin planning October 2017   [SPACE]   ]                |   on the BOARD, not the paper
   +==============================================================================+
```

- **The masthead** is the event name split into heading + period. No new words.
- **The attention line is a rule of the game, so it is set as one**: a stamped left rule, a translucent wash, and the house `[!]` gutter glyph. Not one word of the sentence changed -- it is the frame around it that now says "this is the standing rule".
- **Deltas read as deltas.** `-$36,185` and `-1` are right-aligned in bordered chips, coloured by sign, so a column of them stacks into a readable edge instead of trailing off the end of a sentence. Green/red carry the same meaning as main_ui's per-turn HUD chips (`_DELTA_GOOD` / `_DELTA_BAD`, doom sign-inverted) -- remixed for paper, because colours tuned to survive a near-black panel go washy on manila.
- **Rivals are cards, not three indented lines.** Name and focus on the top line, the drift read underneath in a *heat* ink -- flat is dim, slipping is green, rising is amber, climbing fast is red. Heat, not verdict: it shows which rival is running, which is the one thing three identical sentences could not.
- **The button stays on the board, below the sheet.** The paper is the report, the board is where the action lives. This is also what preserves its B2/B3 teal-on-dark primary chrome -- teal ink on manila would have been unreadable.

### Area

The generic event dialog is a fixed `600x450` (270,000 px^2) at every resolution. The clipboard scales with the viewport, capped at `1120x760`:

| viewport | clipboard | vs. the old panel |
|---|---|---|
| 1920x1080 | 1120 x 760 | **3.15x** |
| 1600x900 | 1120 x 720 | **2.99x** |
| 1280x720 | 921 x 576 | **1.97x** |

Triple where Pip plays, still double on the smallest supported window. Both bounds are pinned by test, the upper one so it cannot creep into a full-screen takeover, and there is a separate test that it never runs off any edge -- it carries the only button that closes it.

### The occlusion

Backdrop `0.6 -> 0.85` **for the review only**; every other event keeps 0.6. At 0.6 the WATCH feed behind the panel still read at close to full strength, so the review looked like it was covering the month it summarises rather than replacing it. At 0.85 the office goes dark and the clipboard is the only lit surface -- which is also what makes it read as an object.

The board carries a real drop shadow (`shadow_size 26`), and that turned out to be load-bearing: without it the panel reads as a flat rectangle again whatever is painted on it.

## Art: what I found and what I used

**Used -- two textures that were already in the pack and referenced by nothing:**

- `res://assets/textures/surfaces/tex_plywood_stained_512.png` -- the board. Stained plywood with grain, spotting and coffee rings.
- `res://assets/textures/surfaces/tex_grid_graphpaper_aged_512.png` -- the sheet. Aged, foxed graph paper with two coffee rings printed into it. This is the whole argument in one asset.

**Nothing was promoted.** Both are pre-existing files under `godot/assets/`, so they were already in the `.pck`; this PR just points at them. A test asserts they are still packed, so retiring either would be caught here rather than silently degrading the panel to a flat fill.

**Surveyed and rejected:** there is **no month/calendar art and no rival-lab art anywhere in the repo**, packed or unpacked. The 64px resource icons (`resource_money_64`, `ui_staff_management_64`, `doom.png`) exist and I looked at them -- they are glossy vignetted RPG icons with baked dark backgrounds, and on a lit manila sheet they read as stickers, not as print. Not used.

**The share/promote route (#1166) is outbound, not inbound.** `tools/assets/build_share_set.py` builds a public candidate manifest from `art_generated/` paths; nothing in it lands in `godot/assets/`. The inbound route is ADR-0019's pull-from-demand pipeline, whose selection file `tools/assets/demand/slot_picks.json` is still empty and whose pull step, by its own README, does not exist yet. Exactly one art file has entered the pack in the last three weeks and it went in by hand. So: nothing to wait for, and I did not promote anything myself.

**What art would finish this**, as a well-specified request rather than a vague one -- both are single-const slots (`BOARD_TEXTURE_PATH` / `PAPER_TEXTURE_PATH`), so a replacement swaps in without touching the layout:

1. **A real clip.** The metal jaw is currently two styleboxes. A drawn clip -- jaw, plate, and a little specular -- is the single detail that would take this from "reads as a clipboard" to "is a clipboard".
2. **Monochrome line-art stamp glyphs, ~24px**, for the Funds / Staff / Doom rows. Flat ink, no baked background, no gloss -- they need to look printed on the form, not pasted onto it.
3. Optional: a purpose-drawn hardboard plate and a sheet with visible tooth. The graph paper works because it is *foxed*; a bright replacement will blow a hole in the palette.

## Scope

**Presentation only.** No numbers, no economy, no phase logic touched. I found no wrong numbers to report.

`game_manager`'s two review blocks are refactored **collect-then-format**: the rows the clipboard draws and the plain text the WATCH feed records (A10) are now built from **one** collection, so the two cannot drift into saying different things about the same month. The emitted text is byte-identical -- the existing `test_month_review_movement` suite passes unchanged against it. Collection runs exactly once per boundary, because the rivals collector advances `_rival_cap_snapshot`.

**ADR-0015 survives the new surface.** The payload carries doom *band labels*, never a percentage, and there is a test that walks the built node tree asserting no `%` reaches the sheet -- a stronger guard than the existing string-level one.

**Every other event dialog is untouched** -- still 600x450, still forest green, still one label of description. The branch turns on one condition (the event carries a `review` payload) and shares everything else: the queue, the blocker lifetime, the button wiring, the `#452` / `#877` / B1 / B2 / B3 metas. There is a test asserting an ordinary crisis window still gets the generic dialog at the original size.

Text is **+2..+4pt on this panel only** per Pip's separate note -- body 16->19, small 14->17, button 16->20. **The masthead is the one exception, 18->24**, flagged in the source rather than smuggled: at 22 it did not read as a masthead beside 19pt body on a sheet with three times the area under it. Easy to pull back if you disagree. No global sweep.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `python3 scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300` | **1352 tests, 0 failures, 131/131 files collected**, exit 0, on the rebased branch |
| tests added by this PR | **20** (measured 1313 -> 1333 before the rebase; main brought the rest) |
| `godot --headless --path godot`, 30s | **zero** `SCRIPT ERROR`, `Parse Error`, `Compile Error`; **zero** `ERROR` lines |
| `python3 tools/check_class_cache.py` | `class cache OK -- 97 class_name declaration(s) all resolve` |
| rebased | onto `origin/main` after #1216 / #1217 / #1220 landed; #1217 also touched `event_dialog.gd` and the merge is clean |

The 20 new tests in `godot/tests/unit/test_month_review_panel.gd` hold the three things a restyle silently breaks -- that **no line of Pip's copy is dropped** by the re-typesetting (it walks the built tree and checks every string is actually rendered), that payload and feed text say the same thing, and that the generic dialog is untouched -- plus the area bounds, the on-screen clamp, the sign convention, the heat/label agreement, and the degradation path when an art slot points nowhere.

Three of them drive the **real presenter** (`EventDialog.present`), not just the builder, so the branch added to `_show_next_event` is exercised end-to-end in a live tree.

## What is NOT verified

**Nobody has looked at this on a screen.** This laptop has no `Xvfb` and no virtual display, and the only real display is the one Pip is playtesting on, so I did not launch a window. Everything above is derived from the source and from tests that inspect the built node tree; **only Pip's eyes can say whether it looks right**, which is the same caveat `test_month_review_navigation.gd` already carries.

To see it:

```
cd /home/pip/Repos/pdoom1-monthreview && make run
```

(worktree at `/home/pip/Repos/pdoom1-monthreview`, branch `feat/month-review-panel` -- Pip's shared checkout at `/home/pip/Repos/pdoom1` was not touched)

**Do not merge** -- Pip reviews first.

`Ladder-Impact: none -- presentation only.` The `game_manager` change is a collect-then-format refactor of two DISPLAY string builders; the emitted text is byte-identical, no RNG is drawn, no state is read that was not read before, and the only new state written is a presentation payload on the review event dictionary. Everything else is under `godot/scripts/ui/`, `godot/tests/` and docs.

issues.title: ADR-0015: runtime pdoom-data event options write literal doom -- an unbounded -6 doom/turn sink
issues.body:
## Summary

The pdoom-data historical events build their player options **in code**
(`godot/autoload/event_service.gd::_generate_options`), so they never went through the
content migration that stripped literal doom deltas from `res://data`. Seven inline
`"doom": +/-N` literals survived there, plus two further vectors in the same file.

Found by Pip in a live playtest ("'diversify funding sources' breaks rules by hardcode
bouncing doom down directly ... this breaks the game by ... creating opportunities to do a
bunch of these and just hard drive doom down to the ground"). He named two; there were nine.

## The literals were not inert

`execute_event_choice`'s ADR-0015 trap (`events.gd:303`) catches a literal `doom` key and
posts it to the **`panic`** stream. So these landed as **real doom, under the wrong name** --
"Conduct internal review" appears in the L6 death chain as panic -- and with **no bound**,
because buffered stream inputs are folded into the rate after `_compute_streams` and so miss
the `maxf(0.0, ...)` hazard clamp.

## Measured

Harness: `godot/tests/unit/test_adr_0015_runtime_doom_literals.gd`.

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| `panic` stream while exploiting | **-6.00 doom/turn** at the shipped 2-events/turn cap |
| with momentum compounding | **-7.78 doom/turn** by turn 20 |
| natural accumulation | +0.06/turn baseline; ~+3.6/turn in the do_nothing calibration |
| result | doom **50 -> 0.0 floor in ~8 turns**, pinned there |
| control (same world, no picks) | doom 50 -> 51.57 over 20 turns |

Supply was never the constraint. Of the 1194 shipped events, **1181 carry a doom-reducing
option**; 1174 are `technical_research_breakthrough` offering `safety_analysis`, which is
**strictly dominant**: 1 Attention, +research, +reputation, -3 doom, no downside. Total
reduction available across the pool is **-3561** against a 0-100 scale, **-339 of it
reachable from turn 1**. Attention (20/month) never binds; the 2-events/turn cap does.

## The nine sites (all `godot/autoload/event_service.gd`)

| option / vector | was |
|---|---|
| `collaborate` (organization) | `"doom": -doom_effect` |
| `build_upon` (research) | `"doom": doom_effect / 2` |
| `safety_analysis` (research) | `"doom": -doom_effect` |
| `support` (policy) | `"doom": -doom_effect` |
| `respond_publicly` (incident) | `"doom": -doom_effect / 2` |
| `internal_review` (incident) | `"doom": -doom_effect` |
| `diversify_funding` (funding) | `"doom": -doom_effect / 2` |
| `_set_default_variable_mapping` legendary bucket | `"doom": 5` |
| `_calculate_base_effects` alias laundering | `vibey_doom`/`stress`/`burnout_risk`/`safety` -> `"doom"` |

The last two sat in the content guard's blind spot: it walks `res://data` only, and it
compares the **raw** impact variable name against `"doom"` literally, so all 1193
`vibey_doom` impacts walked straight past it.

## League relevance

`score == level_reached == turns survived`. The live `(weekly-2026-w33, L4)` board holds one
entry: **109 turns**, `doom_integral` 7931 (mean doom ~27.2, below the 50.0 start), recorded
16:51 on 2026-08-14 under v0.14.1. The calibration's mortality check records **max 26 months
across all policies, 0 immortal runs**. 109 is 4.2x that maximum, with mean doom below the
starting value. Consistent with the exploit; not proof, and it is Pip's own playtest run --
the one in which he found this. **Pip to rule on whether it stands.**

## Fix

PR #1233 routes all nine through named intermediaries, replaces the risk-event count ratchet
with a mechanism rule, and adds a code-side scan.

Note the fix is **ladder-affecting** (`Ladder-Impact: bump` declared, `ladder_version.txt`
left at 4): identical seed + choices now produce a different doom trajectory.

issues.title: fix(doom): route runtime pdoom-data event options through the doom streams (ADR-0015) -- closes a -6 doom/turn sink
issues.body:
Closes #1232.

Pip found this in a live playtest and named two options. There were **nine**, and the exploit
is real: **-6.00 doom/turn**, measured.

## 1. The exploit, quantified

The pdoom-data events build their options **in code** (`event_service.gd::_generate_options`),
so they never went through the migration that stripped literal doom deltas from `res://data`.

The literals were **not inert**. `execute_event_choice`'s ADR-0015 trap (`events.gd:303`)
catches a literal `doom` key and posts it to the **`panic`** stream -- so it landed as real
doom under the **wrong name** ("Conduct internal review" reads as panic in the L6 death
chain), and unbounded: buffered stream inputs are folded in *after* `_compute_streams`, so
they miss the `maxf(0.0, ...)` hazard clamp.

Measured in `test_adr_0015_runtime_doom_literals.gd`:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| `panic` stream while exploiting | **-6.00 doom/turn** at the shipped 2-events/turn cap |
| with momentum | **-7.78 doom/turn** by turn 20 |
| natural accumulation | +0.06/turn baseline; ~+3.6/turn in the do_nothing calibration |
| result | doom **50 -> 0.0 floor in ~8 turns**, pinned |
| control, same world, no picks | doom 50 -> **51.57** |

Supply never binds: **1181 of 1194** shipped events carry a doom-reducing option, 1174 of
them the **strictly dominant** `safety_analysis` (1 Attention, +research, +reputation,
-3 doom, no downside). **-3561** total available against a 0-100 scale; **-339 reachable from
turn 1**. Attention (20/month) is not the constraint; the 2-events/turn cap is.

## 2. How they are routed

| option | now writes |
|---|---|
| `collaborate`, `safety_analysis`, `internal_review`, `support`, `respond_publicly`, `diversify_funding` | `safety_absorption` |
| `build_upon` | `frontier_capability` (its own text says "advancing the research frontier") |
| `_calculate_base_effects` doom, `_default_effects` legendary | `global_panic` |

**Relief goes only to `safety_absorption`, never `global_alarm` -- and that is the whole fix.**
alarm is the engine's designed relief channel and `actions.gd` uses it freely, but those are
*actions*, competing for Attention against the whole board. These options recur on up to 2
events **every turn**, and a repeated input `I` into a decaying stock settles at
`I/(1-decay)`. An early draft of this fix routed `safety_analysis` to alarm and measured a
sustained **-0.84 doom/turn** -- the same exploit in a new costume. `safety_absorption`
cannot do that: overhang is `max(0, frontier_max - safety_absorption)`, so absorption past
the frontier buys **exactly nothing**. The bound is **structural, not a price**.

Two more vectors in the same file, both in the content guard's blind spot (it walks
`res://data` only): the `_default_variable_mapping` legendary bucket still carried
`"doom": 5` after the shipped JSON dropped it; and the variable map launders
`vibey_doom`/`stress`/`burnout_risk`/`safety` into `"doom"` (`vibey_doom` alone is on 1193 of
1194 events) while the guard compares the **raw** name literally.

## 3. MAGNITUDE CHANGED -- your ruling wanted

I did not retune, but I cannot preserve magnitude either, and you should see why:
**the printed literal was ~50x a turn's baseline doom.** Preserving it *is* the exploit --
any routing that reproduces -3 doom per click reproduces -6/turn.

Priced at `doom.streams.event_safety_absorb = 4.0`, reusing the existing
`action_safety_absorb` price rather than inventing a dial. For the dominant case
(`doom_effect = 3`): absorption +12, reducing overhang by `0.000039 * 12` per turn while
frontier exceeds absorption -- about **-0.0066 doom over a 14-month run, versus -3.0 before**.
That is roughly a **450x nerf**, and it is the honest consequence of moving from a printed
number to a modelled stock.

If you want it to bite harder, it is a one-line JSON edit --
`godot/data/balance/defaults.json` -> `doom.streams.event_safety_absorb`. Magnitude-preserving
over a 14-turn run would be **~1832**. I would not go there without a sweep; somewhere in the
tens is my guess for "feels like it did something". **Your call.**

## 4. Sweep -- every doom write outside `doom_system.gd`

**Violating**
- `event_service.gd` x9 -- fixed here.
- `finance_engine.gd:361` `state.add_resources({"doom": -suppress})` -- `desperation_payroll`
  advertises "-10 doom now" and delivers **nothing** (the sink is clobbered at resolve). A
  real violation and a **player-visible lie**, but inert, and its own comment fences it
  ("unchanged pre-L5 path"). **Not fixed here on purpose**: migrating it turns a no-op into a
  real -10 doom, which is a balance change, not a routing fix. Recorded as named debt in the
  new guard so it cannot fade.

**Legitimate** (confirmed, unchanged): the `events.gd` trap; `ledger.gd` -> `ledger` stream
with a test-double fallback; `turn_manager.gd` risk pools -> `add_event_doom`;
`turn_manager.gd:737` the single authoritative sync; `game_state.gd:648` /
`resource_accessor.gd:79` documented inert sinks; `game_manager.gd` resign jam + scenario
start dial; debug-gated nudges in `main_ui.gd` / `dev_mode_overlay.gd`; all `actions.gd`
(fully migrated). Cosmetic only: `conferences.gd` still declares a field named
`doom_reduction` though it correctly feeds `global_alarm`.

## 5. The ratchet loosening (your 18:00 ruling)

`RISK_EVENTS_DOOM_BUDGET := 20` was a proxy, and 20 was exactly the count the day it was
written -- so the real rule became *"no new risk event may carry doom at all, even positive"*.
It failed in **both directions on the same day**: it blocked 28 events of legitimate content
(#1230) while nine literals sat in a `.gd` file it never opens.

Replaced with the rule it stood in for:
- **Data:** no count cap. Risk-pool doom must be **positive** (a pool is a hazard, and it
  routes through `add_event_doom` -> a named stream). **Negative stays illegal everywhere.**
- **Code (new):** the `.gd` tree is scanned for the same defect. Every doom write outside
  `doom_system.gd` is enumerated **with its reason** -- allowlisted as plumbing, or listed as
  known debt. A new write fails and prints its own source line.
- Documented at the head of `test_events.gd`, attributed and dated, so someone finding the
  looser rule in six months can tell a decision from an erosion.

**Both guards proven capable of the other answer:**

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| reintroduce `"doom": -doom_effect` in `event_service.gd` | code scan **RED**, names file + line |
| negative doom in a risk pool | data scan **RED**, names the JSON path |
| **new positive-doom risk event, count 21 (over the old budget of 20)** | **PASSES** |

### What #1230 needs

Its positive-doom risk events now pass as-is -- that last row is the unblock, measured. The
three things it could not express need mechanism it should not invent locally:
"the scare that helps" wants the risk-event apply path to stop dropping intermediary keys
(it silently ignores them today); "regulator pauses a rival" wants an actor id in the event
schema before rival `frontier_capability` is reachable; the invisible `safety_absorption`
payoffs want DQ-21 vocabulary. All three are follow-ups, not blockers. The one hard rule:
**no negative doom literal**, reduce hazard by writing an intermediary.

## 6. Ladder verdict -- EPOCH-SHAPED, your call

`tools/check_ladder_bump.py` goes **RED** without a declaration. This changes the doom
trajectory for identical seed + choices, so it is genuinely ladder-affecting.

I declared `Ladder-Impact: bump` and left `ladder_version.txt` at **4** -- same pattern as
#1230. **I did not cut the epoch**: the `(weekly-2026-w33, L4)` board is being blessed this
afternoon and forking the board key mid-week is yours to decide. Gate is green on the
declaration.

## 7. Could an existing board entry be affected?

**Possibly, and it is worth your attention.** `(weekly-2026-w33, L4)` holds one entry:
**109 turns**, `doom_integral` 7931 -- mean doom **~27.2**, *below* the 50.0 start --
recorded 16:51 today on v0.14.1. The calibration's mortality check records **max 26 months
across all policies, 0 immortal runs**. 109 is **4.2x** that maximum with mean doom under the
starting value, which is the exploit's signature.

Not proof, and it is your own playtest run -- the one where you found this. **Your ruling
whether it stands.** `(weekly-2026-w32, L4)` predates the board and I did not inspect it.

## 8. Verification

- quick: **1346 pass / 0 fail**, 131/131 files (`--quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300`)
- simulation: **107 pass / 0 fail**, 8/8 files
- headless launch: **zero** `SCRIPT ERROR` / `Parse Error` / `Compile Error`; class cache OK
- RED first: the new test fails before the fix on both the structure arm (23 offending
  option/category pairs) and the boundedness arm
- rebased onto `origin/main` after #1216/#1217/#1220/#1222

## Note on process

Two of my early Godot invocations ran **unisolated** -- `CLAUDE.md`'s `APPDATA` rule is
Windows-specific and does nothing here. They wrote logs and touched `keybinds.cfg`/`theme.cfg`
in your real profile. **The league boards were not touched** (`w33` mtime 16:51 predates every
run of mine; contents verified intact, one entry, `pending_scores.json` empty). Switched to
`XDG_DATA_HOME`+`HOME` per `docs/LAPTOP_DEBIAN_SETUP.md` section 4 for everything after.

Not merging -- yours to review.

Ladder-Impact: bump -- doom routing changes the trajectory for identical seed+choices.

issues.title: content(events): 28 new events -- risk grid filled, option counts varied
issues.body:
28 new events for the you-cannot-win-only-buy-time thesis: 18 risk events (every non-minor pool/severity cell doubled) and 10 core popup events with deliberately varied option counts. No doom literals anywhere in the new content.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300` -> **1321 tests, 0 fail** (was 4 fail mid-branch; see "test updates" below -- the gate was run before and after, and it failed before the fixes, so it can return the other answer).
- Headless launch (`godot --headless --path godot --quit`, sandboxed userdata per `docs/LAPTOP_DEBIAN_SETUP.md` section 4): exit 0, **zero** `SCRIPT ERROR` / `Parse Error` / `Compile Error`.
- Both JSON files parse; ASCII-only (no-emoji gate); all effect keys in `HANDLED_EFFECT_KEYS` / risk-path vocabulary; all cost keys payable; ids unique; risk doom-literal count unchanged at 20 (= `RISK_EVENTS_DOOM_BUDGET`).

## Coverage: risk pool x severity (events per cell)

| pool | minor | moderate | severe | catastrophic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| capability_overhang | 2 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 |
| research_integrity | 2 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 |
| regulatory_attention | 2 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 |

| financial_exposure | 2 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 | 1 -> 2 |

The 18 thin cells (exactly one event each) were filled first, as asked. Risk total 30 -> 48.

## Option-count distribution (core events)

| options | before | after | new cohort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 3 | 6 | 3 |
| 3 | 19 | 21 | 2 |
| 4 | 3 | 6 | 3 |
| 5 | 0 | 2 | 2 |

Every new option costs something real (attention, money, research, reputation, papers-forgone, loyalty, a departure, or an intermediary getting worse); each new event keeps one zero-cost-dict out so a broke player is never hard-stuck (existing convention, and `test_cost_display.gd` enforces the free-out-costs-0-AP half of it).

## The doom rule, applied harder than expected

ADR-0015's enforcement in tests is stricter than "no negative literals":

- `test_events.gd::test_no_authored_event_content_writes_literal_doom` fails on ANY `doom` effect outside `risk_events.json`, and caps `risk_events.json` at a shrink-only budget of 20 (the current count). So **new risk events carry no doom literal at all, positive or negative** -- severity is expressed through money/research/compute/papers/reputation/`lose_researcher`, the keys `turn_manager._step_process_risk_pools` actually applies.
- Core events use the ADR-0015 intermediaries (`global_alarm`, `global_panic`, `safety_absorption`, `general_capability`, `frontier_capability`) plus `loyalty_hit` / `lose_researcher`.

### What the rule prevented me writing (design signal, as requested)

1. **The scare that helps.** A near-miss that honestly triggers industry-wide caution (hazard genuinely falls). A reduction must act on a pool or a stream -- but the RISK-event apply path routes only scalar resources; intermediary keys are silently dropped by `add_resources` there. So "the incident that makes everyone more careful" cannot currently be authored as a risk event at all. If the risk path ever learns the intermediary vocabulary, a whole genre opens up.
2. **Severity legibility drift inside a cell.** A new catastrophic event sits next to a legacy one that carries +20 doom; the new one must lean entirely on resource damage. Until the M-ticket migration re-authors the legacy 20, the same cell draws events with structurally different doom behaviour.
3. **"Regulator forces a rival to pause."** The honest effect is a fall in the RIVAL's frontier capability, but the event schema has no actor id -- `frontier_capability` writes address the player slice only -- so the event is inexpressible without a doom literal. Skipped.
4. **A direct doom payoff for adoption wins.** "The industry adopts your eval standard" pays in `safety_absorption`, which is correct -- but the payoff is invisible in option text without printing a doom delta, which ADR-0015 forbids. The intermediary vocabulary for player-facing copy (DQ-21) is what these events are waiting on.

## Test updates forced by the content (4 pre-existing tests)

- `test_risk_system.gd::test_property_all_risk_events_have_doom_effect` asserted **>=50% of risk events carry a literal doom effect** -- the pre-ADR-0015 philosophy, unsatisfiable as content grows under a shrink-only budget. Rewritten as `test_property_all_risk_events_have_teeth`: no effect-less events, plus a local mirror of the 20-cap.
- `test_turn_manager.gd` Key Resignation tests assumed the insider/moderate cell held exactly one event. Added `_pin_risk_cell_to()` so they pin the draw to the event under test; `after_each` reloads the definition cache so the pin cannot leak.
- `weights_request/refuse_request` and `staff_red_line_letter/decline_with_reasons` initially charged 1 Attention and tripped the free-out convention in `test_cost_display.gd`; the attention costs were dropped (both options still carry real effect-side costs).

## Elision proposal (UNACTIONED -- list only, nothing removed, your call)

Candidates that read as old philosophy or previous-workshop templates. History matters; none of these were touched.

1. `talent_recruitment` -- "Fast-Track Hiring" costs strictly more than "Standard Hiring" for the identical effect; a dominated option is a template artifact, not a choice.
2. `funding_windfall` -- both options are pure gains; predates "every mitigation is a loan".
3. `ai_breakthrough` -- a menu of net-positives; the dual-use temptation it gestures at is now priced properly (ADR-0010, and `dual_use_result` in this PR).
4. `media_scandal` -- pay-$40k-to-negate-the-number; pre-ledger shape with no bill later.
5. `harassment_complaint` -- register drifts into HR-simulator gravity, which WORLD_AND_LORE explicitly rules against ("bother", never HR gravity).
6. `mental_health_crisis` -- same HR block, and superseded in spirit by the burnout outcome ruling (prevention cheap, recovery long) now carried by `employee_burnout`.
7. `workplace_conflict` -- duplicate coverage with `risk_insider_minor_2` "Internal Conflict" (same premise, same shape, different file).
8. `office_theft` -- generic office-sim beat with no AI-safety texture; the security lane is better served by `your_security_audit`.
9. `competitor_password_breach` -- the "1234" password gag is a joke-joke rather than institutional comedy; the options are fine, the premise ages the file.
10. `risk_financial_minor_1` "Budget Overrun" -- a bare number bump (-$15k, no texture); the thinnest event in either file.

## Notes for review

- **Event density:** 10 new random core events raise per-turn qualifying counts. Probabilities are kept at 0.04-0.05 and `MAX_NEW_EVENTS_PER_TURN = 2` spreads the burst, but pool density is the parked design call in #578/#579 -- worth an eye during the next playtest.
- **Ladder:** new event content changes which events fire on a seed (the textbook Section 3.1 trigger). `ladder_version.txt` is deliberately untouched -- the epoch cut is yours to time against the league roll.

Ladder-Impact: bump -- new event content changes which events fire on a seed; epoch cut itself deferred to Pip at merge (league-roll cadence), ladder_version.txt untouched here.

Do not merge without Pip's review (admin-merge flow).

issues.title: Playthrough of this afternoon's build: music works, save looks better -- but settings traps you into quitting, F3 will not close, and the cold open never fired
issues.body:
**From:** coordination seat · **Source:** Pip voice memo `2026-08-06_140157__c11e34d1`, recorded 14:01 AEST playing **the fresh build made this afternoon** — *"was meant to be fixing a few things."* Live play, narrated as it happened. Transcribed locally; quotes are ASR output, lightly punctuated.

## Core message

**The music system works and the save looks much better.** Two navigation defects made him quit the game entirely to get out of a menu, and **the cold open did not fire on any of three attempts**, so it remains unverified rather than working.

## Two navigation defects, one of which forced a quit

**1. Settings has no exit except "back to game" — so from the main menu it is a trap.**

> I can't go from settings to quit, I can only go back to game. So now if I go back to game, I have to quit. **I'm just going to quit out entirely, that sucked.**

Reached from the main menu, Settings offers a route that assumes a game is running. He had to close the application.

**2. `F3` does not toggle, and the overlay cannot be dismissed.**

> clicking F3 again doesn't work, clicking out of F3 using the X works, backslash doesn't bring anything up

So `F3` opens but does not close, and one documented dismissal path is dead while another works.

## The cold open did not fire — three attempts

He tried the sequence three times, twice deliberately re-entering via settings to enable story entries:

> Settings, all protocols, play story entries on, front card, back to game — that's not going to work. Main menu, launch lab, launch lab... **I did not get the intro, so I can't confirm whether the intro worked or not.**

**Treat the cold open as unverified, not as working.** Whatever the fresh build changed, he could not reach it. Worth checking whether the story-entries setting actually gates it, and whether it persists across the settings round-trip he was forced into by defect 1.

## Music — works, one refinement

Confirmed working after some confusion: *"Excellent, okay — no, the music works."* Selecting a track and pressing play works; selecting a second and playing switches correctly.

**The one fix:** *"we need to make it more clear that the track is fading over and that it takes a few seconds"* — the crossfade reads as unresponsiveness. He was otherwise enjoying it.

## Player guide — better, one structural note

*"How to play is good, the month is good, attention and resources"* — all fine, and he likes that money, compute, research papers and reputation are now **coloured**, with a caveat: *"I don't know if those colourings are consistent, but if they are then that's kind of cool."* **Worth confirming those four colours are used consistently everywhere**, because he is about to rely on them.

Structural note: *"these are all scrollable little mid-sections, as opposed to one long continuous scroll, which is weird."*

## Leaderboard — a concrete request

> it would be cool on the leaderboards to be able to **sort them — by date, or duration, or turns** — just have that dropdown filter once the information is loaded.

Sorting client-side after load, not a new query. This composes with the leaderboard work in the teardown response.

## Small observations

**Staff cards grow slightly on click** when planning to interview — *"a weird little on-click effect"*, noted as funny rather than wrong.

**The phase-one event error is now handled.** Previously this produced an unrecoverable state; now *"I get a nice little error message in the background."* Still cannot resolve, but it no longer traps him — the earlier report in `#1132` can be considered improved, though the underlying dev-tool boundary question stands.

## Not tested, deliberately

He intended to test offline behaviour and decided against it mid-session: *"I'm not going to turn off the network because I'm just doing too many other things, we'll deal with that other thing later."* **Network-loss behaviour remains untested.**

issues.body:
**Design thread, deliberately NOT work.** Pip said *"not now"* about this in the same
breath as describing it, and it is filed so the direction exists as a durable thing to
argue with rather than a paragraph in a playtest file. Nothing here is scheduled and
nothing here is a request.

The reason it is worth filing at all is that **most of it already exists**, and knowing
that changes what the conversation is about.

---

## The direction, as he described it

People behaviours -- sitting, standing, fetching things, the printer, the fridge. Trash
accumulating over time. Janitors to collect it. And, zoomed out, an XCOM-style view of a
lab network showing the organisation growing.

## What already ships -- and the screenshot is the live game, not a mock

The 2026-08-14 16:21 screenshot shows a floor with tables, props and two name-labelled
staff figures (Iris Wilson, Quinn Patel). **That is `OfficeFloor`, running on the WATCH
screen in the real build.** `watch_screen.gd:30-76` instantiates
`godot/scenes/ui/office_floor/office_floor.tscn` in code and labels it
*"Office floor -- N staff:"*; `main_ui.gd:1124-1125` refreshes it on every
`game_state_updated`. The names come from `Researcher._generate_name_with_rng`
(`researcher.gd:261-273`).

**One correction worth making early, because it changes cost estimates: it is top-down,
not isometric.** `grep -rn -i isometric` across `godot/scripts`, `godot/scenes` and
`godot/data` returns exactly one hit -- a parenthetical in a comment at
`office_floor/render_grid.gd:57`. The grid look is a Wang-atlas concrete floor tile. Going
isometric is a renderer rewrite, not a camera change.

**4,793 lines already exist** under `godot/scripts/ui/office_floor/`:

| File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `office_sandbox.gd` | 2291 | dev-only toy; small/large office compare, prop placement, cats, doom-glow POC. Never ships. |
| `employee_sprite.gd` | 843 | one walker: FSM art, micro-behaviours, separation steering, 8-direction facing |
| `office_floor.gd` | 833 | the shipped view; floor, props, tables, roster diffing, desk layout |
| `render_grid.gd` | 357 | first-class `Vector2i` render grid |
| `anchored_overlay.gd` | 202 | socket-anchored overlays |
| `worker_variant_pool.gd` | 114 | per-worker appearance variants |
| `employee_fsm.gd` | 57 | pure state mapping, headless-testable |

Backed by **16 unit test files** (`test_employee_fsm`, `test_office_walker_separation`,
`test_office_no_stand_in_footprint`, `test_office_floor_facing`, `test_render_grid`,
`test_prop_manifest`, ...).

### The behaviours he asked for are partly built

The figures are not static. `EmployeeFSM.map_state()` (`employee_fsm.gd:33-47`) maps a
snapshot to one of four states with explicit precedence -- `stressed` (burnout >= 80),
`walking` (unmanaged), `idle` (loyalty <= 15, checked out), `working` (assigned), `idle`
default. On top of that `employee_sprite.gd` runs cosmetic micro-behaviours off `_process`
(`:593`) with sub-states `desk | to_break | on_break | to_collab | collaborating |
returning` (`:174`):

- a working employee takes **food runs to the fridge or water cooler**, or goes to pat the
  cat, then returns
- **peer-desk collaboration**, initiated by `OfficeFloor.try_start_collaboration()`
  (`office_floor.gd:310`)
- a `walking` (unmanaged) employee does `drift | window | spin` (`:180`) -- window-gazing
  and spinning on the spot, so disengagement reads visually
- boids-lite separation steering between walkers and cats, strength 40 deliberately below
  walk speed 42 so it cannot deadlock

**Sit, stand, fetch and the fridge are shipped. The printer is not. Trash and janitors are
not.**

### The office economy is shipped too

`godot/scripts/core/office.gd` (195 lines) + `godot/data/office/offices.json`. Tier 0 is
"Bedroom / basement", `hire_cap: 2`, rent 0 -- and **the forcing function is the cap, not a
modal**: the third person has nowhere to sit. Three tier-1 leases (Pip's 2026-07-27 ruling,
"3 offices to choose from"): `coworking_corner` (cap 4, $4,500/mo), `walkup_office`
(cap 7, $9,000/mo), `university_annex` (cap 9, $6,000/mo). Wired end to end -- lease offers
through `FinanceEngine`, rent on the monthly payroll rail (`month_controller.gd:403`),
hiring blocked by `Office.has_desk_space` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:283`). No moving mechanic in
v1: once signed, the lease is locked.

**So the buy/rent office workshop Pip mentioned has a mechanic to workshop against, not a
blank page.** `#791` is the open issue and
`docs/game-design/OFFICE_ECONOMY_PROPOSAL.md` is the written proposal. That proposal's
section 2d already suggests the tier-1 signing as a `startup_era -> office_era` flip -- and
notes that `OfficeFloor` does not currently read the signed lease at all. The accessor was
built for it: `office.gd:25-27` says `floorplan()` exists "purely so office_floor.gd can
size itself off the signed lease *later*". **Making the office visibly grow when you sign a
lease is the single cheapest item in this whole direction**, and it is most of what "a view
showing the organisation growing" would deliver.

### Art: the bottleneck is promotion, not generation

`godot/assets/office_floor/` holds 353 files, 174 PNG, 5 SpriteFrames -- 5 worker variants
with full directional sets. But **`props/` contains exactly three PNGs**
(`filing_cabinet`, `server_cluster`, `water_cooler`), matching a 3-entry
`godot/data/office/props_manifest.json`, and `tilesets/` contains **one**. The tables and
desks in the screenshot are drawn procedurally (`draw_circle` / `draw_rect`,
`office_floor.gd:722-731`), not art.

Meanwhile `art_source/` holds **4,457 PNG**, including unpromoted prop, worker and cat
sweeps (`pixellab_2026-07-27_prop_rebase`, `pixellab_2026-07-26_prop_grain_vanguard`,
`pixellab_2026-07-27_t6_worker_diagonals`). **A printer, a bin, a whiteboard and a coffee
machine are very likely already generated.** Same promotion story as `#1166`.

## Janitors and trash: already ruled, and parked deliberately

Not a gap -- a decision. Zero hits for janitor / cleanliness / trash in `godot/scripts` or
`godot/data`. Pip, 2026-07-25, `docs/game-design/SEED_RIVAL_AND_DEVELOPMENTS.md:153-168`:

> It was a proof of concept money sink about 1,300 commits ago. abandon mechanism, lightly
> hold onto mechanical idea. I am thinking here of little people walking around SimPark and
> reliably dropping trash that a little janitor would wander around and collect, but at a
> lower scale / probably only relevant once we get larger offices, maybe?

The old `office_maintenance` action (paid $5,000, did nothing) was removed in v0.13.1.
`OFFICE_ECONOMY_PROPOSAL.md:327` lists janitor/ambient upkeep as explicitly out of scope,
tier 2+ office-era content, "the seed stays parked". **That is the same idea returning in
the same words a month later, which is a signal about its durability, not a reason to
unpark it.**

The same doc, `:324-326`, pre-rules the adjacent temptation: office quality may surface as
flavour and later as a pricing input, **never a mood engine** -- *"'bother,' not HR
gravity"*.

## The live constraint any proposal must be written against

`docs/game-design/decisions/ADR-0018-render-only-office-doctrine.md`. Pip, verbatim:

> No spatial fact will ever become a gameplay input.

The sim owns counts and quantities; the render owns coordinates. Rider (b) makes
render-local cosmetic interaction unrestricted -- clicking a coffee pot, idle poses -- and
rider (c) allows click-the-render to dispatch a sim action provided it serialises as
`(action, entity_id)` and never coordinates, with a non-spatial path always available.
Rider (a) sets a re-review date.

**So: fetch-the-printer, trash piling up, a janitor walking a route -- all legal as pure
render.** What is not legal is desk-placement bonuses, pathfinding as gameplay, or
cleanliness as a hidden stat feeding productivity. An "XCOM base view" in the sense of
*placing rooms to get effects* is ruled out today. In the sense of *a zoomed-out picture of
what you have built* it is not, and it is the version `floorplan()` was left open for.

`docs/game-design/BUILD_BRIEF_PLAN_WATCH_UI.md:74-108` already lays out the ladder:
**Tier 0 and Tier 1 are DONE.** Tier 2 is specified and explicitly marked *plan, do NOT
build* -- hand-authored `NavigationRegion2D` work-zones, a utility/blackboard layer for
contextual pair behaviours, and a global event-reaction hook (everyone glances up on a doom
spike). **Tier 3 -- LLM-driven generative agents, Smallville-style -- is ruled OUT, not a
stretch goal**, because it breaks replay determinism. Lines 108-112 defer costumes and the
"office-as-moral-mirror" idea (office aesthetic reflecting upgrades, moral path and doom)
and ask for an `office_tier` / `moral_skew` seam.

For the record, **no document in this repo uses "XCOM" for the office view.** The word
appears 20+ times, always for art direction (StarCraft 2 x XCOM matte-painting) or recruit
attachment (`DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY.md:342`). The base-view framing is new with this playtest and
is worth keeping distinct from the existing usage.

## What this thread is for

Not a build. When it is picked up, the questions worth an hour are:

1. **Does the office read the lease?** Signing a tier-1 lease and watching the room change
   is the growth feeling, it is pure render, and the seam is already open.
2. **Which Tier 2 behaviours earn their cost**, given Tier 1 already does fridge runs,
   collaboration and window-gazing. The printer is one sprite and one waypoint.
3. **Does trash return as pure render**, with no cleanliness stat -- ambient decoration that
   scales with headcount and gets swept by a walker? That version is ADR-0018-legal and does
   not unpark the mechanic.
4. **What "zoomed out" means** if it is not room placement. A lab network, a headcount
   silhouette, a floor that grows.

## Related

- `docs/game-design/decisions/ADR-0018-render-only-office-doctrine.md` -- the binding
  constraint.
- `docs/game-design/BUILD_BRIEF_PLAN_WATCH_UI.md:74-112` -- the tier ladder; Tier 2 spec,
  Tier 3 ruled out.
- `docs/game-design/OFFICE_ECONOMY_PROPOSAL.md` -- lease/floor-space proposal, janitors
  out of scope at `:327`.
- `docs/game-design/SEED_RIVAL_AND_DEVELOPMENTS.md:153-168` -- the janitor seed, parked in
  Pip's own words.
- `#1202` item 4 -- Pip naming office sim on both screens as the day's priority, with the
  ADR-0018 constraint attached.
- `#1140` -- persistent office simulator on both screens, not updating during planning,
  playing out as the queue drains.
- `#925` -- office W3 pre-build: tile-grid addressing, prop placement metadata, room layout
  format, office-fullness primitive. The engineering substrate.
- `#791` -- early lease economy. `#467` / `#471` -- outfitting and cosmetic shopping.
- `#793` -- staff sprite variety and scale. `#913` -- office juice. `#924` -- cat
  animations. `#1091` -- arrivals come through a door, the first real staff behaviour tied
  to a sim event.
- `#1092` -- events name physical things the office never shows; the prop-promotion route.

issues.title: Events: 25 authored, 19 of them the same three-option shape, and the taxonomy built to vary them is used by zero of them

labels.name: strategic
labels.description: Strategic planning and high-level architectural decisions

issues.body:
From the 2026-08-14 playtest. Pip wants more events. This issue is the measurement that
turns that into a scoped ask, and it reports something more interesting than a low count:
**the events we have are all the same shape, and the machinery built to make them
different shapes is used by exactly zero of them.**

Every number below came from a command run against the tree, not an estimate.

---

## The census

Three corpora, and the issue is about the first one:

| Corpus | File | Count | Carries authored options? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hand-authored core events** | `godot/data/events/core_events.json` | **25** | yes, all 25 |
| Risk-pool events | `godot/data/events/risk_events.json` | 30 (6 pools x 4 tiers) | **none** -- pure effect blobs |
| Historical corpus (pdoom-data) | `godot/data/historical_events.json` | 1194 | **none** -- options synthesised at runtime from `category` |

1174 of the 1194 are `technical_research_breakthrough` (the arxiv flood), demoted to the
feed tier where "their effects are never applied and no decision opens"
(`docs/decision-cards/2026-08-02_pdoom-data-contract.md:73`). **So the number of events
that ask the player a question is 25.**

**Option-count distribution over those 25:**

```
2 options:  3   (funding_windfall, rival_poaching, media_scandal)
3 options: 19
4 options:  3   (employee_burnout, whistleblower_approach, competitor_password_breach)
```

Every one of the 25 is `"type": "popup"`. The union of option-level keys across all 25 is
`costs, effects, id, message, text`. **Nineteen events with exactly three options and one
uniform shape is not a content library, it is a template used nineteen times** -- and that,
rather than the raw count, is what a player feels as sameness.

## The finding that should change the plan: the taxonomy is built and unused

A `window` block is a real, optional per-event dictionary read by
`WindowResolver.window_config()` (`godot/scripts/core/window_resolver.gd:25-26`), with four
recognised sub-keys, all defaulted:

- `attention_cost` (default `DEFAULT_ATTENTION_COST = 1`, `:22, :30`)
- `handle_option` (default: the first option, `:33-42`)
- `ignore_option` (default: the first zero-cost option, else the last, `:45-57`)
- `lapse_penalty` (opt out of the automatic ignore-reputation penalty, `:118-120`)

It sits alongside `delivery_tier`, `event_class`, `source_id`, `unignorable` and
`expiry_turns`, all documented at `godot/scripts/core/event_tiers.gd:3-22`.

**Measured: I walked all 40 JSON files under `godot/data/` for a `"window"` key at any
depth. Zero occurrences.** Likewise `delivery_tier` appears in **zero** of the 10 files in
`godot/data/events/`; the only one in the whole data tree is the default at
`godot/data/balance/defaults.json:7`.

The 25 open as windows anyway, by a legacy fallback: `type == "popup"` plus non-empty
`options` -> `TIER_WINDOW` (`event_tiers.gd:52-54`). **Which means all 25 run on default
Attention cost 1, the default handle option, the default ignore option, and the default
`deferrable` class.** The ADR-0012 taxonomy -- un-snoozable, standing, no-action, expiry,
unignorable, per-event Attention pricing -- is implemented, unit-tested, and exercised by
no shipped event data at all.

**Same story for cannibalise.** `grep -ril "cannibali" godot/data/` -> **0 files**;
`grep -ril "cannibali" godot/` -> 16 files, all code, tests and docs. It is an engine
response verb (`window_resolver.gd:5-11`, `MonthPlan.pay_by_cannibalizing()` at
`month_plan.gd:354`, legality per class at `event_tiers.gd:96-104`), and the only place a
window is constructed with the verbs wired is runtime GDScript --
`hiring_pipeline.gd:591-604` and `:623-636`. **No authored event opts into it.** Read
alongside `#1221`, which establishes that the cannibalise path has no production WIP
registry to pull from either: right now the verb is offered by two hiring cards, refuses
in the voice of a rule, and no event data uses it.

## So: is adding events cheap? Yes. Suspiciously so.

There is **no "how to author an event" document.** I grepped `docs/`, `docs/design/`,
`docs/game-design/`, `docs/content/`. What exists is adjacent:
`docs/EVENT_OVERRIDE_SYSTEM.md` (the historical-corpus override pipeline),
`godot/data/events/overrides/README.md`, `docs/design/EVENT_PROMOTION_PASS.md` (which says
at `:150` that "You choose a decision by choosing a TEMPLATE (category), not by authoring"
one), and `event_tiers.gd:1-22` as the de-facto schema doc.

The **actual** surface for a new core event is: append one object to the `events` array.
Loader is `GameEvents.get_all_events()` (`events.gd:38-50`), which only expands
`{cost_money}`-style templates. Required keys, per the only test that checks
(`godot/tests/unit/simulation/test_events.gd:18-27`): **`id, name, description, type,
trigger_type, options`** -- six. Everything else is optional with defaults.

Three content rules a new event must survive:

1. **`test_event_affordable_out.gd`** -- every choice event must offer an option costing
   neither money nor Attention. (The one real design constraint, and a good one.)
2. **`test_events.gd`** -- no literal `doom` key in effects (ADR-0015). `risk_events.json`
   has a grandfathered budget of exactly 20 which "MUST only ever go down".
3. Repo gates -- ASCII-only, no emoji (`scripts/check_no_emoji.py` blocks on
   `godot/data/**/*.json`).

**Fifty more events is a JSON append, zero code changes, zero schema registration.** Which
means the cost of this work is entirely in writing, and the shape of it should be decided
before anyone writes fifty more copies of the three-option template.

## Hardware events assume hardware, and the condition language cannot say otherwise

Pip's point, confirmed. Three of the 25 are hardware/compute-adjacent, plus one that sells
equipment. **None gates on owning any:**

| Event | Text | Gate | `min_turn` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `technical_failure` | *"Your compute infrastructure suffered a major failure!"*, options Emergency Repair / Basic Fix / *"Run on degraded hardware"* | `money >= 20000` | 12 |
| `office_theft` | *"Expensive equipment has disappeared from the lab"*, option "Install Security System" | **none at all** | 15 |
| `compute_deal` | +100/+150 compute | **none** | 6 |
| `funding_crisis` | option "Sell Lab Equipment", +$120,000 | `money < 50000` | 10 |

A two-person bedroom lab that has bought no infrastructure has its compute infrastructure
suffer a major failure, and can sell equipment it never owned.

**This is not a content fix.** `GameEvents.evaluate_condition` (`events.gd:193-250`) splits
the condition string on spaces and reads exactly `parts[0] parts[1] parts[2]` -- one
resource, one operator, one number. The resource must be one of **13 hardcoded names** in
`ResourceAccessor.has_readable` (`resource_accessor.gd:12-19`): `money, compute, research,
papers, reputation, doom, attention, safety_researchers, capability_researchers,
compute_engineers, managers, researchers, total_staff`, plus the special case
`salary_disparity`. **There is no `has_upgrade(...)`, no office tier, no boolean of any
kind.** Gating hardware events on hardware requires extending the condition grammar.

Note too that `compute` starts at **100.0** for every run
(`defaults.json`, `starting_resources.compute`), so "compute exists" is trivially always
true. The hardware that genuinely may not exist is the `hpc_cluster` ($800k),
`upgrade_computer` ($200k) and `secure_cloud` upgrades -- **and no event references any of
them.**

### Defect found while verifying: two conditions are silently truncated

`evaluate_condition` has no `and` handling anywhere. Two shipped events carry compound
conditions:

- `funding_windfall` -- `"papers >= 3 and reputation >= 40"` (`core_events.json:141`)
- `research_leak` -- `"researchers >= 3 and research >= 10"` (`core_events.json:715`)

Replicating the parser: both evaluate as `papers >= 3` / `researchers >= 3`, with
`['and', 'reputation', '>=', '40']` and `['and', 'research', '>=', '10']` **discarded with
no warning**. The reputation and research halves of those gates have never fired. This is
the same class as `#1215` -- a silent wrong answer from something that looks like it is
working -- and the cheap guard is a validation test that rejects any
`trigger_condition` the parser cannot fully consume.

## Pip's outreach idea -- keep this, it is the best content lead in the notes

He proposed asking operations Slacks for **anonymised real project disasters**, to be laced
in behind the research-paradigm upgrade path. That is the same instinct as `#1016`
(*provenance real infrastructure failure modes into the event history as flavour text /
metadata*), aimed at a different source, and it is a much better answer to "the events feel
samey" than authoring fifty more three-option templates in-house. It also has a
guardrail already written: `docs/game-design/WORLD_AND_LORE.md:36, 58` -- flavours, never
portraits of real people.

## What this issue is actually asking for

1. **Decide the shape question before the volume question.** Nineteen identical templates
   is the complaint; a 26th would be a twentieth.
2. **Use the taxonomy that exists.** Put `window` blocks, `delivery_tier`, `event_class`,
   `expiry_turns` and `unignorable` into real event data, even on a handful, so the machinery
   is exercised by something other than tests. Per-event Attention pricing alone would
   differentiate a crisis from a memo.
3. **Extend the condition grammar** enough to say "you own an HPC cluster", then gate the
   four hardware events. Cheapest honest version: add `has_upgrade` and an office-tier read
   to `ResourceAccessor`.
4. **Fix the silent `and` truncation** and add the guard.
5. **Run the outreach.** Anonymised disasters from real operations people, behind the
   research-paradigm path.

**Resolve `#1193` first.** It asks whether the current event density is intended after
`#1137`'s retiming made a simulated run ~38% more expensive. If the answer is "too dense",
that argues for *better* events, not more, and this issue's item 1 becomes the whole of it.

## Related

- `#1193` -- event density after the retiming. **Read first.**
- `#579` -- *"event pool too small / frequency off; expand pool or check the mechanic"* --
  the existing statement of the complaint, from workshop 2.
- `#825` -- OUTS sweep: every response offers a resource trade-off, no dead ends. The
  `affordable out` test is its enforced half.
- `#986` -- risk_events re-author + rebalance (20 live fields).
- `#615` -- Build lane L4, event taxonomy + ledger intake (ADR-0012). The taxonomy this
  issue reports as unused is that lane's output.
- `#1016` -- provenance real infrastructure failure modes as event flavour. The outreach
  idea's existing home.
- `#595` -- audit options/events/buttons that cost but have no meaningful impact. The
  hardware-gating item is a precondition-shaped sibling.
- `#1092` -- events name physical things the office never shows. The art-side inverse of
  the hardware finding.
- `#1221` -- refusals must say rule-or-stub. The cannibalise verb is the worked example.

issues.title: Design: the ledger and research progress both stop at the edge of the roster -- one missing object (a paper with contributors) blocks both

labels.description: Strategic planning and high-level architectural decisions

issues.body:
**Design issue, not a bug.** From the 2026-08-14 playtest. Two of Pip's asks that arrived
as separate thoughts and turn out to be one missing object.

His first, on the ledger -- and he named it as the biggest thing:

> the biggest promise of complexity we don't mechanically connect... maybe the ledger will
> then let staff remind their bosses "hey, don't forget you owe me c-lead on a paper soon"

His second, on research:

> Civ-style -- seeing how far a paper is, so keeping a researcher becomes a real decision

Filed together because **both bounce off the same absence: there is no paper object with
contributors.** The ledger cannot owe a named person a co-lead credit, and the player
cannot see a paper approaching, for exactly the same reason -- a paper is not a thing in
this game until the moment it exists, and then it is a `+1` on a counter.

This is the same pattern as playtest note 5 (`coordination/DESIGN_2026-08-12_interrupt-resolution-variants.md`,
Variant C): **Pip reproduced in play a need that the design record already answers on
paper.** That is validation of the design, not a new requirement. Both halves below are
already written down; what follows is what shipped instead.

---

## Part 1 -- the ledger is built, and it does not know that people exist

`docs/game-design/decisions/ADR-0003-liability-ledger.md`, **Status: ACCEPTED as design;
build first among the new systems**, dated 2026-07-04. Pip is right that the engine is
built: `godot/scripts/core/ledger.gd` is 505 lines, with a real `Entry` class (`:21-72`),
ten live currencies in `_bill` (`:213-295` -- `money`, `reputation`, `governance`, `doom`,
`papers`, `compute`, `attention`, and the inert standing terms `equity` / `board_seat` /
`agenda`), a balance block (`godot/data/balance/defaults.json:29-52`), a player-facing
screen, and thirteen distinct entry factories.

Three of ADR-0003's load-bearing promises did not survive the build.

### 1a. "The ledger is two-sided" -- it is one-sided

> **The ledger is two-sided:** Payables -- what you owe... **Receivables** -- favors and
> pledges owed *to you*, held **per-actor**. **Influence is not a resource** (decided by
> Pip): there is no global influence number; there is leverage over *this* lab, a favor
> owed by *that* actor. Receivables carry **counterparty risk** -- a pledge is not a vote
> until cast.
> -- ADR-0003:32-40

**`Side.RECEIVABLE` is never constructed anywhere** in `godot/scripts/` or `godot/tests/`.
Every occurrence is a read (`ledger.gd:485`, `ledger_screen.gd:187`,
`dev_mode_readout.gd:137`). The ledger screen's `Favors:` figure is structurally always
`$0`. The seam is even parked in a comment -- conference contacts "become a Ledger
counterparty entry post adoption-v1" with `"receivable": null` hardcoded at
`conference_trip.gd:378`.

### 1b. A person cannot be a counterparty

The `counterparty` field (`ledger.gd:30`) is written in exactly four places, all in
`finance_engine.gd` (`:339, :345, :392`), and always to an institution: `"bank"`, `"vc"`,
`"philanthropy"`, `"commercial_agent"`. Every people-flavoured factory --
`staff_rider` (`:121`), `appetite_promise` (`:150`), `resentment_debt` (`:172`) -- calls
`Entry.new` with five arguments and leaves `counterparty` at its `""` default. The field is
also **not rendered in the player-facing ledger at all**: the columns are
`Source | Amount | Due | Notes` (`ledger_screen.gd:218, 230-236`). Only the dev overlay
prints it.

**People currently exist in the ledger as substrings.** `appetite_promise` encodes the
person into the `source` string as `"promise:<id>:<name>"` (`ledger.gd:155`), and
`_settle_promise` (`:333-358`) -- the only code in the ledger that reads a person back --
recovers them by `e.source.split(":", true, 2)` and scanning `state.researchers` for a name
match, with a defensive comment about names containing colons. It then moves that
researcher's loyalty: **+3 kept, -8 broken.**

That loyalty delta is the whole of the mechanical connection between the ledger and the
roster. It is real, and it is the seed of exactly what Pip described.

### 1c. The one promise that IS owed to a person settles against a global counter

The offer dialog can already promise `first_authorship`, and it already prices it honestly:
*"owes 1 first-author paper slot in ~10 turns"* (`ledger.gd:162-168`, rendered at
`hiring_panel_controller.gd:518-520`). This is good work and it is nearly the feature.

**But `first_authorship` bills `state.papers`** (`ledger.gd:264-274`, `PROMISE_SPEC` at
`:143-148`) -- the global fungible counter. **The promise is discharged by any paper
existing.** Nothing records that the promisee authored anything, because:

- `PaperSubmission.lead_researcher_name` and `co_author_names` exist as fields
  (`paper_submissions.gd:46-47`) and serialize.
- `lead_researcher_name` is written in **exactly one place in the entire codebase**:
  `actions.gd:934`, at conference-submit time.
- **`co_author_names` is never written by any gameplay code.** Grep over `godot/scripts/`
  returns the declaration and the serializer, nothing else.
- `calculate_paper_quality` takes a `co_author_count` parameter
  (`paper_submissions.gd:140`, bonus at `:148-149`) whose only caller passes the literal
  `0` (`actions.gd:921`).
- There is no c-lead, co-lead or shared-credit concept anywhere. The nearest thing is
  flavour text: `godot/data/researchers/quirks.json:100`, *"An authorship dispute lands on
  your desk."*

So the exact sentence Pip wants a researcher to be able to say -- *"you owe me c-lead on a
paper soon"* -- has no object to point at.

### 1d. Two smaller findings, recorded here so they are not lost

- **The `attention` currency has no producer.** No factory mints it; the branch at
  `ledger.gd:284` is reachable only via `from_dict` rehydration. This is item C of `#1218`,
  which also notes it is the only currency arm that never calls `_note(...)`, so it would
  produce no cause-log attribution if it did fire.
- **`reputation` is now dead too.** The comment at `ledger.gd:131-142` records why:
  promises were re-homed off raw reputation after a single promise's bill zeroed a
  50-point reputation bar and killed a real run on turn 14.
- **The file's own docs are stale.** `ledger.gd:7` and `:24` both list the currencies as
  "money, reputation, governance, attention, doom" -- omitting `papers`, `compute`,
  `equity`, `board_seat`, `agenda`. Worth a `class:docs` fix regardless of what happens to
  the design.

---

## Part 2 -- a player cannot see a paper coming, and could not attribute it if they could

### 2a. Progress is `research mod 100`, and it is shown to nobody

The shipped research model is a single global float. `_step_researcher_productivity`
(`turn_manager.gd:149-294`) rolls per researcher per turn -- `research_roll < 0.30 *
productivity` (`:208-211`), amount `randi_range(1,3)` (`:212`), times research multiplier
and specialization (`:213-220`) -- and sums **all of it into one anonymous local**
(`research_from_employees`, `:164, :239`). `_step_publish_papers` (`:615-634`) then converts
at `papers.research_per_paper = 100.0`, keeping the remainder with `fmod`.

**There is no per-paper object during accumulation.** "Progress toward the next paper" is
literally `state.research mod 100`.

**Definitive verdict on visibility: a player cannot see how close a paper is, anywhere, by
any means.**

- HUD renders `"Research: %s"` and `"Papers: %s"` as raw scalars (`main_ui.gd:1149-1150`).
- The only disclosure of the threshold is a hover tooltip -- *"Generated by staff. %d
  research = 1 auto-published paper."* (`main_ui.gd:789-791`). A player who hovers can do
  the division by hand. No bar, no percentage, no "next paper in N".
- **The only `ProgressBar` in the entire UI layer is the hiring panel's onboarding
  checklist.**
- The only per-paper display in the game is the conference panel
  (`travel_panel_controller.gd:189-215`), which shows discrete *status* -- Under Review /
  Accepted / Rejected -- not progress, and those Path-B papers never touch the `Papers`
  counter.
- Employee screens show the input and never the output: `Skill Level: N/10`,
  `Productivity: N%` (`employee_screen.gd:340-346`). Nothing shows what a person is working
  on or what they have contributed.

**So losing a researcher is invisible as a loss.** Nothing attributes any part of
`state.research` to a person. The roster shows a productivity percentage and never what
that productivity produced, or what stops when they leave. That is precisely Pip's point:
keeping a researcher cannot be a real decision while their absence has no legible shape.

### 2b. The object that would fix both parts already exists and is unreachable

`godot/scripts/core/workstream.gd` is a complete implementation of the missing primitive:
`effort_accrued` / `effort_target` (`:64-65`), `duration_months`, `assigned_ids`,
**`contributions: Dictionary` mapping researcher_id -> float (`:68`)**,
`progress() -> float` 0.0..1.0 (`:175-179`), **`lead_contributor()` (`:193-205`)**, and a
`readout_line()` that already formats a percentage (`:241-247`). Accrual is wired into the
turn loop at `turn_manager.gd:296-354`.

**No workstream can ever be started in a real run.** `GameState.start_workstream`
(`game_state.gd:883-896`), `assign_to_workstream` (`:926-938`) and `available_backlog`
(`:874-880`) have **zero callers outside `godot/tests/unit/test_workstream.gd`** -- no
action id, no UI, no data hook. The turn step's own docstring admits it:

> It is also INERT on an untouched run: with no workstreams started, nothing is billed to
> compute and only bookkeeping tallies move.
> -- `turn_manager.gd:310-312`

`grep -rn "workstream" godot/scripts/ui/` returns **zero hits** -- not even in the dev
overlay.

And the intent that would answer Pip's exact question is already coded, on that unreachable
path:

> A departing person stops accruing, but what they already contributed STAYS on the
> workstream... Losing your lead is supposed to hurt as a slowdown, not as a retroactive
> erasure.
> -- `game_state.gd:849-852`

---

## Why this is one issue

The unreachable `Workstream` has `contributions` and `lead_contributor()`. The ledger's
`first_authorship` promise needs exactly a contributor record to settle against. The player
wants a progress bar, which `Workstream.progress()` already returns. **Wiring one object
answers both asks**; wiring neither is why they both appeared in the same hour of play.

The order that follows from the above -- offered as a starting point, not a ruling:

1. **Make `Workstream` reachable at all** (an action id and a panel). Everything else is
   downstream and nothing else is possible before it.
2. **Show `progress()`** on the WATCH surface. `docs/game-design/BUILD_BRIEF_PLAN_WATCH_UI.md:66`
   already asks for "progress bars and completion ticks" on the in-flight queue.
3. **Settle `first_authorship` against a contributor record** rather than `state.papers`, so
   the promise means what its own cost text says.
4. **Then, and only then, receivables** -- a named person holding a claim on you is the
   two-sided ledger ADR-0003 specified, and it is the thing Pip described in play.

## Related -- read these instead of re-deriving them

- `docs/game-design/decisions/ADR-0003-liability-ledger.md` -- the ruling. Sections quoted
  above.
- `docs/game-design/decisions/ADR-0011-effort-economy.md:26-29, 42-44` -- the single ADR
  that already links both halves: staff effort -> workstreams -> papers, and
  *"promises made to retain staff are ledger entries"*.
- `docs/game-design/RESEARCH_IDEA_PAPER_PIPELINE_GAP.md` -- the definitive prior analysis
  (2026-07-22), including the link-by-link verdict table at `:123-129` and three build
  options at `:227-296`. **Its `file:line` appendix (`:312-333`) is now stale** -- it cites
  `turn_manager.gd:119-250`/`:480-500` and `main_ui.gd:547`, which are today `:149-294`,
  `:615-634` and `:789-791`.
- `docs/game-design/BUILD_BRIEF_HIRING_PIPELINE.md:56-57` -- already specifies the promise
  half: *"a prestige-hungry candidate takes less cash for a first-authorship promise (mints
  a ledger entry, ADR-0003)"*, and `:90` lists Ledger promises/retention debts as a system
  this wave touches.
- `#833` -- the people & money cohesion spine (`docs/game-design/PEOPLE_AND_MONEY_COHESION.md`).
  This issue is the ledger/research face of that spine, measured after the hiring pipeline
  shipped. If #833 is the container, this can be folded into it -- but the measurements
  above are new.
- `#1044` -- *actions resolve instantly, so the early game has no rhythm*, item 3: the queue
  should promise a completion time. Relevant caveat for part 2: a progress bar over
  instant-resolving work has nothing to show. **Research is not in that category** -- it
  accrues per turn already (`turn_manager.gd:149-294`), which is precisely why it is the
  one thing in the game that could carry a progress bar today.
- `#615` -- Build lane L4, event taxonomy + ledger intake (ADR-0012).
- `#614` -- Build lane L3, adoption/papers/conferences (ADR-0010, ADR-0014).
- DQ-14 "World-state progression display" (`docs/game-design/WORKSHOP_2_BACKLOG.md:60-62`,
  indexed open at `DQ_INDEX.md:23`) -- the nearest existing home for part 2's complaint.
- `#578` item 3 -- researcher info on the hire screen.

issues.title: Firing exists -- on a screen the player never reaches, and it is the one departure that costs nothing but cash
